sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

items.prompt: A line has equation y = 2x - 1. Which of these equations represents a line parallel to it?

steps: Parallel lines have the same slope but different y-intercepts.
y = 2x + 4 has slope 2, the same as y = 2x - 1, but a different intercept.
So y = 2x + 4 is parallel to the given line.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: A line has equation y = -6x + 11. Write the equation of the line through (-5, 42) that is parallel to this line.
A plant's height is given by H = 3w + 8, where H is the height in centimeters and w is the number of weeks since it was measured. What does the slope represent in this context?
choices: The plant was 8 centimeters tall when it was first measured.
The plant grows 3 centimeters per week.
The plant grows 8 centimeters per week.
The plant was 3 centimeters tall when it was first measured.

items.prompt: The amount of water in a tank is given by G = 1t + 4, where G is the number of gallons in the tank and t is the number of minutes since filling started. What does the y-intercept represent in this context?
choices: The tank fills at a rate of 4 gallons per minute.
The tank already had 1 gallons of water before filling started.
The tank fills at a rate of 1 gallons per minute.
The tank already had 4 gallons of water before filling started.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: Find the slope of the line through (-13, -6) and (-16, -18).
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt:
A line passes through these points:
x: 16, 19, 22
y: -12, -2, 8
What is the slope (rate of change) of the line?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A line passes through (10, 10). A slope triangle on the line has a horizontal leg (run) of 4 and a vertical leg (rise) of -3. A similar slope triangle further along the same line is 4 times as large. Which point also lies on the line?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
